additions.site_name: Unit 4, Silverdale Industrial Estate, Silverdale Road, Hayes (London Borough of Hillingdon)
additions.name: Silverdale Road data centre, Hayes - new data centre building with emergency generator (Hillingdon 49261/APP/2024/2904)

status.summary: On 22 October 2026 the London Borough of Hillingdon approved details (49261/APP/2026/2094) pursuant to Condition 25 (Air Quality Assessment) of planning permission 49261/APP/2024/2904, dated 12 March 2026, for the demolition of the existing building at Unit 4, Silverdale Industrial Estate, Silverdale Road, Hayes and the construction of a data centre building (Class B8) with roof-level plant, one emergency generator and flue, sprinkler tank and pumphouse, security guard house, a kiosk substation and MV building, access road, parking and landscaping. The council's dated approval shows the data-centre permission is an issued, live consent: it is the sixth condition approval on it since May 2026, after the construction management, low emission strategy, contaminated land, flood risk, materials and landscape details. Permitted status is supported as of 22 October 2026. No demolition, construction or operation is established; the condition approved here must precede installation of the generator, but no works are inferred from it.
status.permit_reference: London Borough of Hillingdon full planning permission 49261/APP/2024/2904 (dated 12 March 2026 per the council's condition records), with approval of details 49261/APP/2026/2094 under Condition 25 decided 2026-10-22
status.permit_identity_review: The 22 October 2026 register entry approves details 'pursuant to the discharge of Condition 25 (Air Quality Assessment) of planning permission ref. 49261/APP/2024/2904 dated 12-03-2026' and restates the permitted development as the construction of a data centre building (Class B8) with roof plant and an emergency generator at Unit 4, Silverdale Industrial Estate, Silverdale Road, Hayes. The council's register entry for 49261/APP/2024/2904 shows status 'Approval' for the same proposal and location, and the London Planning Datahub record of that permission carries its decision conditions, which restrict the development to use 'as a data centre' and require an operator declaration and generator testing schedule before operation. The consent therefore covers the data-centre building itself, not only enabling or utility works. No appeal, challenge, revocation or later superseding permission was found.

status.summary: The Royal Borough of Greenwich's record 26/2370/EIA, published through the Greater London Authority's London Planning Datahub, shows that on 14 October 2026 the council issued (delegated decision 'Approved') its Environmental Impact Assessment scoping opinion on a request, validated on 7 August 2026, for a proposed 100,000 sq m GEA data centre with ancillary offices, internal plant and substations, alongside up to 10,000 sq m GEA of mixed employment and community space, on land adjacent to and including the former Stone Foundries, 669A Woolwich Road and the VIP Industrial Estate, Charlton SE7. The scheme described has a data centre of up to 45 m AOD and retains the Stone Foundry building. This dated council record identifies the proposed data-centre development, supporting announced status as of 14 October 2026. A scoping opinion is neither a planning application nor a consent; no permission, site work or construction is asserted, and no applicant or operator is named.
